About LuminX

Warehouses still run on clipboards and barcode guns. Every day, billions of dollars in pallets move through docks where humans manually scan, count, and verify — and when something goes wrong, no one notices until a customer complains.


LuminX is changing that. We build AI camera systems that watch every pallet move in real time, read every label and barcode automatically, and surface errors the moment they happen. We're already deployed with major customers in automotive and cold storage, and we're growing quickly. We raised $5.5M in seed funding from top investors and have a senior team that includes alumni from leading robotics and AI companies.


The Role



We’re hiring a Robotics Systems Engineer to own the software and systems that run on our edge AI devices—the embedded compute, cameras, device software, and hardware integrations that make LuminX work in customer warehouses. You’ll spend most of your time on the edge stack, but you’re a hands-on generalist at heart, comfortable moving between software, hardware, and field deployment when the problem calls for it.


Our devices live in real warehouses with real power, networking, temperature, and physical constraints. Debugging at the hardware-software boundary is part of the job, not a side quest. You do not need to be an electrical or mechanical engineer, but you should be comfortable tracing a wiring issue, testing or replacing a component, adjusting a mount, bringing up new hardware, or traveling to a customer site to get a system working.

Develop and maintain software running on NVIDIA Jetson and Rockchip-based edge devices.
Integrate and troubleshoot cameras, sensors, networking equipment, storage, and other peripherals.
Build device services for camera capture, health monitoring, telemetry, configuration, and remote management.
Diagnose issues across Linux, device software, networking, power, and hardware integration.
Create tools for device provisioning, testing, deployment, logging, and over-the-air updates.
Support the bring-up and validation of new edge hardware.
Work with the ML team to deploy and evaluate models on edge devices.
Work with the hardware team to improve device reliability, installation, and serviceability.
Travel to customer sites to support installations and diagnose issues.
Turn lessons from field deployments into better software, tooling, and system design.


What We're Looking For

3+ years of experience in robotics, embedded systems, computer engineering, or a similar hands-on engineering role.
Experience working with embedded Linux or edge computing platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson, Rockchip, or Raspberry Pi.
Proficiency in Python, C++, or both.
Comfort working in Linux and debugging processes, logs, system services, networking, and connected devices.
Experience integrating cameras, sensors, compute modules, or other physical hardware.
A practical understanding of wiring, power, connectors, and basic electrical troubleshooting.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to diagnose issues across multiple parts of a system.
Willingness to perform hands-on work and occasionally travel to customer sites.
A high degree of ownership and comfort working in an early-stage startup environment.


Bonus Points For

Experience with JetPack, CUDA, TensorRT, or DeepStream.
Experience with Rockchip platforms, including RK3588.
Familiarity with camera interfaces such as MIPI CSI, USB3, GigE, GMSL, or V4L2.

About the Role
Anthropic's inference fleet serves Claude to millions of users across our own products and the world's largest cloud platforms. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, model servers, distributed routing, autoscaling, capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation.

The Inference System Dynamics team is responsible for understanding that whole system and holding it to a high bar across four dimensions: throughput, latency, reliability, and correctness. We measure how the fleet performs against its theoretical performance frontier, run cross-layer investigations to explain the gaps, and own the correctness checks that make sure Claude's outputs are right, not just fast, across hardware platforms and serving configurations. We don't own the individual components. We instrument and model them, find the highest-leverage opportunities across them, and partner with the owning teams to land the wins.

You'll work across all four areas. One week that might mean tracing a tail-latency regression from request timing down through routing and batching into a kernel overhead; the next it might mean tightening a correctness eval so it catches an output regression introduced by a quantization change. We're looking for performance engineers who treat correctness as part of performance.

Key Responsibilities
Run cross-layer performance investigations across throughput, latency, and reliability, sizing the gap between actual fleet performance and theoretical rooflines, identifying root causes, and quantifying the value of closing them
Own and improve the correctness evaluation pipeline that validates model output quality across hardware platforms, numerics, and serving configurations, and lead the investigation when it catches a regression
Build the observability, dashboards, and modeling tools that make throughput, latency, cost, reliability, correctness, and their interactions legible across the stack
Partner with kernel, serving, routing, autoscaling, and capacity teams to prioritize and land the highest-impact optimizations your analysis surfaces
Ruthlessly stack-rank a large surface area of opportunities by impact and effort, and say no to the ones that don't make the cut

Ability to communicate quantitative results clearly in writing to influence priorities on teams you don't manage
Genuine interest in correctness as an engineering discipline: numerics, evaluation design, regression detection

Familiarity with GPU/TPU/accelerator performance concepts (memory bandwidth, kernel overheads, quantization, collective communication). Reasoning about these matters more than having written kernels yourself
Experience with reliability engineering for high-throughput services: autoscaling, load balancing, request routing, tail latency
Experience with model evaluation or numerical regression-detection pipelines
Experience building observability or telemetry for distributed systems

Location: Fremont, CA - Onsite

We are seeking a Product Quality & Reliability Engineer, in Fremont, CA to serve as the technical quality lead for Nextpower's robotic and electronic systems. This role owns product-level quality from design through field performance, ensuring seamless integration of hardware, firmware, and electromechanical subsystems. Partnering cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, and suppliers, this individual will embed quality early in the product lifecycle, lead reliability validation and NPI activities, and drive data-driven improvements across PCBA, motion control, sensor, and embedded systems. The ideal candidate combines strong electronics and mechatronics expertise with hands-on validation experience, supplier quality leadership, and a passion for building robust, high-performing products.

Responsibilities:

 

Product Quality Ownership

Serve as the technical quality lead for robotic and electronic products—ensuring hardware, firmware, and electromechanical integration meet Nextracker standards.

Partner with design, test, and manufacturing engineering to embed quality and reliability controls early in the product lifecycle.

Define, implement, and validate product test and inspection requirements across PCBA, harness, motion control, and sensor subsystems.

Support new product introduction (NPI) through DFMEA/PFMEA execution, control plan creation, and design verification test (DVT) oversight.

Validate and qualify test systems and automated inspection tools for functional verification of complex assemblies.

Drive product-level reliability testing (HALT, HASS, burn-in, and environmental stress screening) and feed results into design improvements.

 

Supplier & Component Quality

Evaluate and approve suppliers for electronic and robotic assemblies—PCBs, actuators, control boards, sensors, and embedded systems.

Audit supplier facilities to confirm process capability, traceability, and quality control for critical components.

Lead technical reviews on defect trends, early-life failure data, and product field returns (RMA/FA), driving corrective and preventive action.

Implement statistical process control (SPC) and advanced data analytics (Cp, Cpk, Weibull, X̄-R) to monitor and improve part and system performance.

Develop, implement, and maintain supplier quality scorecards with metrics that emphasize reliability and system performance consistency.

 

Cross-Functional Leadership 

Collaborate with hardware and software teams to validate design for manufacturability, serviceability, and long-term reliability.

Translate customer and field feedback into actionable product improvement initiatives.

Support failure investigations through structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5-Why, fault tree analysis) and ensure learnings are applied to future designs.

Champion the “design for quality” mindset across the product organization—linking field performance data directly to design and supplier improvements.

  

REQUIREMENTS 

 

Bachelor’s Degree required (prefer degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Robotics Engineering).

Experience: 3–7 years in product-level quality or reliability engineering for robotics, embedded electronics, or smart devices.

Strong working knowledge of PCBA design and testing, motion control systems, sensors, and firmware integration.

Experience in product validation, DVT/PVT processes, and environmental/reliability qualification testing.

Skilled in Minitab or similar SPC tools, with the ability to interpret product data and drive measurable improvements.

Knowledge of ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or ISO 13485, with hands-on experience in supplier or product audits.

Proficient in GD&T, AQL inspection, and problem-solving frameworks such as DMAIC or DFSS.

 

Language:           Fluent in English

Travel:                  Up to 50% domestic travel, international travel may be required

Work Visa:          Authorized to work in United States 

 

INTERPERSONAL SKILLS 

 

·         Analytical and innovative problem-solver with strong technical grounding in electronics and mechatronics.

·         Skilled communicator who can engage effectively with design, manufacturing, and supplier teams.

·         Naturally curious, driven to understand how products fail and how to make them more robust.

·         Comfortable in both lab and field environments, balancing data analysis with hands-on validation.

·         Adaptable, pragmatic, and capable of leading cross-functional efforts under tight deadlines.

·         Committed to quality excellence, product reliability, and continuous improvement.

About the Company 

At Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business. 
A leader in autonomous driving since 2007, Torc has spent over a decade commercializing our solutions with experienced partners. Now a part of the Daimler family, we are focused solely on developing software for automated trucks to transform how the world moves freight. 
Join us and catapult your career with the company that helped pioneer autonomous technology, and the first AV software company with the vision to partner directly with a truck manufacturer. 

Meet the Team 

Torc is developing Level 4 autonomous semi-truck software to transform how freight moves across the world. As a Software Engineer I on the Test Automation team, you will support the development of automated validation systems used to verify software releases across embedded and autonomy platforms using Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) systems. 

This team focuses on validating software early in the development lifecycle by building scalable automation frameworks and validation infrastructure that improve release quality and system reliability before deployment onto vehicles. In this role, you will work closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams to support automated testing workflows, debug issues across hardware and software systems, and contribute to the continuous improvement of Torc’s validation infrastructure. 

Your work will directly contribute to the safety, reliability, and scalability of Torc’s autonomous driving platform.

Develop Python-based tooling supporting test automation, validation workflows, and data analysis  
Support execution and monitoring of automated software validation across embedded and autonomy subsystems  
Assist in analyzing test failures, debugging issues, and investigating root causes across hardware and software components  
Collaborate with systems, embedded, and autonomy teams to support validation strategies and improve test coverage  
Help maintain scalable test infrastructure and CI-based validation workflows  
Support integration and verification activities involving sensors, compute platforms, and control systems  
Participate in test planning, automation improvements, and validation activities across the software development lifecycle

Strong programming experience in Python  
Familiarity with software development workflows including version control, build systems, or CI/CD environments  
Basic understanding of embedded systems, robotics systems, or hardware/software integration concepts  
Ability to analyze logs, debug issues, and troubleshoot software or system-level problems  
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced team environment  
Strong communication skills and willingness to learn in an evolving technical environment

The Role
As a Vehicle Validation Engineer at Wayve, you’ll play a key role in enabling the real-world deployment of our end-to-end AI driving systems. You’ll ensure our vehicles are ready for testing and that test activities deliver high-quality, reliable data to accelerate development.

Joining at an early stage, you’ll help shape how we test and operate autonomous vehicles at scale—developing validation approaches, improving systems, and working closely with engineering, product, and operations teams to push the boundaries of what’s possible.

Beyond test execution, you’ll contribute to how vehicle performance is evaluated and communicated, helping provide meaningful feedback on system behaviour, performance gaps, and real-world driving quality from a customer perspective.

Key responsibilities:

Plan and execute vehicle tests to support development, validation, benchmarking, and real-world deployment.
Develop and improve vehicle validation test concepts to evaluate system performance across a range of real-world scenarios.
Work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams to translate testing needs into effective test activities.
Ensure vehicles are prepared, maintained, and consistently ready for safe and efficient testing.
Deliver high-quality test data, performance reporting, and actionable insights to support rapid iteration and decision-making.
Provide detailed feedback on vehicle behaviour, driving performance, and system gaps from both technical and customer perspectives.
Conduct benchmarking activities to evaluate system performance and track progress over time.
Develop and improve testing processes, documentation, and operational best practices as the team scales.
Manage relationships with external suppliers and service partners.

You’re a hands-on engineer who thrives in fast-moving environments and enjoys working at the intersection of hardware, software, and real-world systems. You take ownership, focus on outcomes, and look for ways to continuously improve how things are done.

Essential Skills & Experience

Experience with CANalyzer, CANoe, or similar tools for vehicle diagnostics, along with vehicle instrumentation and data logging tools (e.g. Vector, ETAS, Racelogic).
Experience executing structured vehicle tests in proving ground and/or real-world environments.
Comfortable working across Linux, Windows, and SSH-based environments.
Ability to interpret technical requirements and translate them into clear test cases and validation plans.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, product, and operations teams.
Proactive, hands-on approach with a focus on improving processes, tools, and ways of working.
Understanding of safe testing practices and risk assessments in safety-critical environments.
Ability to analyse test data and deliver clear, actionable insights to engineering teams.
Desirable Skills & Experience

Experience working with autonomous vehicle or ADAS systems.
Familiarity with scripting or data tools (e.g. Python, MATLAB) for analysis or automation.
Understanding of vehicle networks (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and diagnostic protocols.
Exposure to simulation or test environments (e.g. HiL, SiL).
Awareness of automotive safety standards or regulatory frameworks (e.g. ISO 26262).
